text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Citibank opened a subsidiary in Bucharest and is now awaiting its clients for retail banking services.
- Romanian medicine importers said they lost 11 billion lei in two months because of the depreciation of the leu currency.
- Electricity utility Renel RA said the outstanding debt of thermal authority Radet was 87 billion lei on January 1.
ADEVARUL
- Health Minister Stefan Dragulescu plans to raise physicians' monthly wages by 59 percent.
- The Finance Ministry worked out a draft law on a three-year exemption of farm income taxes in a bid to support the macro-economic stabilisation programme.
- South Korean concern Daewoo will continue to reinvest the money it makes in Romania, shows a press release following statements on Daewoo made by Senate chairman Petre Roman.
- The price of bread is expected to go up by 50 percent starting February 10.
ZIUA
- Reform is Romania's last chance, said Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea during a press conference on Thursday on Romania's talks with international lenders.
LIBERTATEA
- Private entrepreneurs in Romania complain about irregularities on the over-the-counter market and say the capital market might get blocked under thinning investor confidence.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Travel agencies demand the elimination of a hard currency rule saying Romanians travelling abroad can exchange the equivalent of $500 annually.
- Forestry authority Romsilva RA plans to sign a contract with U.S. company Tenneco to harvest wood in less accessible areas.
- Banca Agricola RA will raise interest rates in leu deposits starting February 1.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The amendments to law on the restitution of houses nationalised by the former communist regime breach electoral promises, the paper says.
- Fund shortages hit imports of medicines and affect the population's health, said participants in a conference organised by the paper.
- The liberalisation of hotel tariffs could have a negative effect on the tourism sector, the paper says.
- Romania's former king Michael wants to return to his native country "soon", Michael's aid George Antoniade says in an interview.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's Supreme Defence Council decided to create a special task force to be deployed alongside NATO troops for emergency situations and peacekeeping missions.
- A possible return of ex-king Michael to Romania should be the result of a political decision, Senate chairman Petre Roman is quoted as saying.
LIBERATEA
- Gangs of gypsies make handsome profits by allegedly extorting street vendors of "protection taxes".
- Lack of funds prevent attempts by the former ruling Party of Social Democracy to buy the private Tele7 ABC television station, the paper says.
- Each jail inmate costs taxpayers 2.6 million lei a year.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Ion Diaconescu, head of the National Peasant Party, denies rumours of an imminent visit by king Michael to Romania.
- Genady Seleznyov, head of Russia's Duma, says in an interview that Russia would oppose NATO enlargement plans.
- Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica asked prosecutors to step up investigations in cases of corruption.
-- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
